threads.body: [General] `built()` only reads this thread-local target; it does not remove it. After the outer SRV settings are built, a callback that reenters with a non-SRV `MongoClientURI` (for which this method returns `null`) or builds `ClusterSettings` directly before the outer advice exits will therefore still have its settings overwritten with the stale outer SRV target. Consume and remove the target when `built()` reads it, while retaining `close()` cleanup for paths that fail before a build, and cover the non-SRV nested case.

replies.body:
Addressed in 0d53d5b52a4186cf4af91e1d5e766ce595522946.

Analysis: `built()` now removes the thread-local target immediately after reading it. `LegacySrvTargetScope.close()` still removes an unconsumed target when construction fails before a build. The regression test confirms that a nested non-SRV construction uses its own direct target after the outer SRV settings are built.

Upsides: Reentrant non-SRV or direct settings builds cannot inherit a stale SRV target.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [General] On MongoDB 3.7, both the mongo-3.1 and mongo-3.7 modules advise the same `ClusterSettings.Builder#build()` and call `built()` for the same settings instance. The first call consumes the legacy SRV handoff and records it, but the second sees no handoff and overwrites that configuration with the builder's resolved-host configuration. This can make a legacy `MongoClientURI` SRV client report resolved hosts instead of its SRV target. Make `built()` idempotent for each `ClusterSettings` instance so later advice calls preserve the first result.

threads.body: [General] This handoff is not safe if legacy `createCluster` is reentered before the outer builder reaches `build()` (for example, through an overridden `MongoClientURI` getter). A nested non-SRV call returns `false` without masking the outer target, so its builder consumes the outer target; a nested SRV call overwrites the outer target instead. Carry a scoped previous value through `@Advice.Enter`, install the current operation's target even when it is null, consume the current value in `built()`, and restore the previous value on exit. This preserves an unconsumed outer handoff without restoring one that was already consumed.
